title: Apply for a provisional rider licence (serviced area)
summary: Learn how to apply for a provisional rider licence in a serviced area after completing the required pre-provisional rider training course.
intro:
To upgrade to a provisional rider licence in a serviced area, you must first undertake the pre-provisional rider training course.

The course is a full-day course and includes a one-hour motorcycle operator skills test (MOST). When you successfully complete the course you'll be issued with a pre-provisional certificate of competence to take to your local Service NSW Centre.

The certificate is valid for 3 months.

When you visit the service centre, you can apply for a NSW Photo Card at the same time if you wish, and take advantage of paying a reduced application fee for it.
who_can_apply: Have held a learner rider licence for at least 3 months.
Have successfully completed the pre-provisional rider training course with an approved motorcycle training provider.
what_you_need: Your contact lenses or glasses (if you wear them)

how_to_steps.text: Complete the form and check the tick box to apply for a NSW Photo Card (if applicable).
Visit a service centre and lodge your application with your payment.

more_info.text: For rider licence applications, a receipt is provided which allows you to ride until the card arrives in the mail. The receipt is valid for 2 months.
The NSW Photo Card is voluntary – you don't have to have one, but you may find it useful to prove your identity in situations not related to riding/driving.

faqs.q: What is required before applying for a provisional rider licence?
faqs.a: You must first complete the pre-provisional rider training course, which includes a one-hour motorcycle operator skills test (MOST).

faqs.q: How long is the pre-provisional certificate of competence valid for?
faqs.a: The certificate is valid for 3 months.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to apply for the licence?
faqs.a: You need the 'Licence Application' PDF form, your pre-provisional certificate of competence, your learner rider licence, your contact lenses or glasses (if applicable), a current concession card (if applicable), and your payment.
